title: The stone house is built

cast.P_HUSBAND: the householder (invented): Romano-British man of local stock, about 40, lean, dark brown hair cut short, short dark beard, grey-green eyes, a weathered outdoor face, a small old scar on the chin; undyed natural wool tunic to the knee with a narrow brown border, a plain dark-green wool cloak pinned at the right shoulder with a plain bronze penannular brooch
cast.P_WIFE: his wife (invented): Romano-British woman, about 35, chestnut-brown hair parted in the middle and pinned up at the back, oval face, dark eyes, freckles across the nose; a long saffron-yellow wool dress, a dark-blue wool shawl, no jewellery but a plain bronze bracelet

cast_rule: New faces for the 2nd century: never the Iron Age couple, the old door-2 AD 200 couple (K_FARMER_AD200/L_WIFE_AD200) or the c. AD 220 cast (R_*). Portraits bible/cast/roman150_{husband,wife}.jpg made once and reused for en/es.
language_rule: BIBLE PERIOD ACCURACY rule 4: Brittonic is lost, so modern Welsh is spoken as its closest living descendant and the opening card says so once; Latin is not spoken (the household is local Romano-British); a few Welsh words that came from Latin in this period are used where natural (calch < calx). Welsh and Spanish machine-written, for native review.
subtitles_rule: cy/en/es; Welsh cues start [in Welsh] in en/es; <=2x42 chars, <=20 cps, 0.83-7 s (subtitle_check.py)
no_fourth_wall: No narrator, no archivist, no Grandson; characters speak only to each other; side facts as captions only.
dialogue_rule: Lines carry no facts beyond the sources: everyday words of a household watching its stone house go up; builders have no lines.

lines.speaker: P_WIFE
lines.en: Look at it. A house of stone, up here on top of the hill.
lines.cy: Edrych arno fe. Tŷ o gerrig, lan fan hyn ar ben y bryn.
lines.es: Miralo. Una casa de piedra, acá arriba, en lo alto de la loma.

lines.speaker: P_HUSBAND
lines.en: Stone lasts. Timber rots and thatch burns. This will stand long after we're gone.
lines.cy: Ma' cerrig yn para. Ma' pren yn pydru a gwellt yn llosgi. Fe safith hwn ar ôl i ni fynd.
lines.es: La piedra dura. La madera se pudre y la paja se quema. Esto va a quedar en pie cuando ya no estemos.
lines.accent: South Wales (Welsh standing in for Brittonic)
